breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Bottom navigation and floating compose button give way to an icon-only left rail; the feed column caps at 600px with hairline sides on the paper ground.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The rail gains labels (15rem) and the 20rem side panel with people search appears.

full.purpose: Avatars, postmark, buttons (pills, and 48px icon circles), close button, rail items, bottom-nav current-page pill.

scroll.purpose: Locking scroll for a modal never shifts the page sideways.

icons.purpose: Line icons, aria-hidden, in the current text colour; never emoji or Unicode glyphs.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action on a screen ("Chirp", "Sign in"): an airmail red pill, 44px (36px small). Hover 95% brightness, pressed 90%; loading keeps full colour with a centred spinner.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Every other action ("Follow", "Cancel"): sheet pill with a hairline border; hover takes the paper wash.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Quiet actions in toolbars, menus and modal cancels: faded ink text, no fill; hover takes the paper wash and ink.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Confirms something destructive ("Delete chirp"). Outlined at rest so it never reads as the primary action; hover fills with danger and on-danger text.

components.name: Text field
components.description: Labelled 44px input, 8px radius, field-border outline (ink on hover, danger when invalid); hint in faded ink; error is an alert icon plus text in danger.

components.name: Modal

narrative.overview:
Every chirp is a letter from someone you chose, stamped with the moment it was sent. The world borrows from airmail correspondence: a blue-tinted paper ground, navy ink, the red-and-blue chevron of an airmail envelope, and a round postmark that carries each chirp's time. By night the envelope turns over: a navy ground with paper-tinted ink, the same red and blue lifted so they still pass AA.

Chirp runs in Operate mode. The world lends type, palette, density and one signature move; layout, navigation and controls stay the familiar social-app ones (timeline, composer, profile, follow lists), so nobody needs onboarding. Calm comes from restraint: flat sheets separated by hairlines, one accent per job, and absolute time instead of a ticking "2m".

The surface is dense in the way a phone feed must be (a 44px avatar, 15px body, 12px row padding) but never crowded; the postmark is the only ornament inside a chirp, and the chevron is the only ornament on the page.
keyCharacteristics: Airmail paper and navy ink by day, a navy envelope by night, both following `prefers-color-scheme` through `light-dark()`.
Airmail red for the one primary action and the liked state; airmail blue for links, selection, focus and the postmark ring.
One chevron hairline, under the header, and nowhere else.
Flat: hairline dividers, no decorative shadows; one soft float shadow only for things that hover above the page.
Archivo Variable throughout, tabular figures wherever numbers sit.
Every chirp carries a postmark: day first, 24-hour time, tilted about 6°.

rules.name: The Red Letter Rule
rules.body: Airmail red marks the one primary action and the liked state, nothing else. If a second red element appears on a screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Blue Pen Rule
rules.body: Airmail blue means "you can go here or you are here": links, selection, focus and the postmark. It never fills a button.

rules.name: The Not By Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: No state is carried by colour alone: a liked chirp changes its icon and its accessible state as well as turning red; errors carry an icon and words.

rules.name: The AA Both Ways Rule
rules.body: Every foreground/background pair passes WCAG AA in both themes. A new token ships with its day and night ratios checked, not just its day one.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Wherever digits sit (times, counts, dates, the character counter) they use tabular figures, so columns of numbers and the postmark do not jitter.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo Variable is the only typeface. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and tracking, never from a second display face.

rules.name: The Full Bleed Feed Rule
rules.body: Feed rows run edge to edge on the sheet and are separated by hairlines. They are never cards, and never cards inside cards.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from hairlines and the paper/sheet step. The only shadow is `shadow-float`, and it belongs only to things that float above the page (toasts and the phone's compose button); a modal is set apart by the scrim instead. No other shadow exists in this world: not on cards, rows, buttons, fields or menus at rest.

rules.name: The One Chevron Rule
rules.body: Exactly one chevron hairline per page, under the header. It is the page's only edging; it never frames cards, buttons or dialogs.

dos: **Do** define every new colour as a `light-dark()` pair on `:root` and map it through `@theme inline`, then check its AA ratio in both themes.
**Do** keep airmail red to the one primary action and the liked state.
**Do** use airmail blue for links, selection, focus and the postmark ring.
**Do** separate feed rows with 1px hairlines on the sheet, full bleed.
**Do** use tabular figures for every time, count and date.
**Do** postmark chirps day first ("21 NOV") with 24-hour time, and expose the full date to assistive technology inside `<time datetime>`.
**Do** pair every colour-coded state with an icon change, text or `aria-pressed`.
**Do** let `prefers-reduced-motion` reduce every animation and transition to effectively zero.
**Do** build screens from the primitives (Button, ButtonLink, Avatar, Field, Modal, Spinner, EmptyState) and show toasts only through `notify`, after any open modal has closed.
**Do** confirm destructive actions with the outlined danger button.
**Do** keep a busy button at full colour with its spinner; fade only buttons that are genuinely disabled.
**Do** draw icons from Lucide at a 1.75 stroke.
**Do** mark the current page with `aria-current`, a bolder label and the paper pill as well as airmail blue.

**Do** write each error as one message that names the problem and what to do ("Use at least 3 characters"), never repeating the field's hint; put problems no single field owns in the form alert at the top of the form.
donts: **Don't** add a second chevron edge or use the chevron as a frame; there is exactly one, under the header.
**Don't** use decorative shadows; depth is paper, sheet and hairline, and `shadow-float` is reserved for things that float (toasts, the phone's compose button).
**Don't** wrap feed rows in cards, or nest cards inside cards.
**Don't** fill buttons with airmail blue or use red for anything but the primary action and the liked state.
**Don't** fill the danger button at rest; it is outlined so it never competes with the primary action.
**Don't** carry a state by colour alone.
**Don't** replace the postmark with relative "2m" labels as the only sense of time.
**Don't** use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons.
**Don't** use X's name, bird mark or brand blue.
